title: Hold every hookable Remote Claude, and show and release a held chat
body:
Context: commits bdf3877 and 54648b5 (read both bodies), docs/remote-sessions.md, docs/agent-state.md, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (The way back, Agent state, Results). Foreman delivers chat by pasting into the agent's pane and sending Enter after ready::SUBMIT_DELAY; that only works when the agent sits at its input box. 54648b5 added a chat hold for a hooked Remote Claude (ReadyGate::hold, remote::ChatHold, remote::chat_hold, remote::note_route, claude_with_hooks, prompt_index).
THE HUMAN'S REQUIREMENT, verbatim intent: a clean production-ready implementation that is PROVEN working. Reproduce each defect first by driving the real application, record the outcome, fix it, then drive the real application again and record that the defect is gone. A unit test alone proves nothing here. If you cannot reproduce a defect, say so with the runs you made and do not invent a fix for it.
How to drive the real application. Test Remote: andy@192.168.8.168 (hostname Falador, Debian, key login; never ask for a password; Claude Code and Codex installed, Grok not). You run inside the INSTALLED foreman, which lacks these changes; never stop any foreman by name and never touch an instance you did not start. Build your own: cargo build --release --target-dir target/agent/hooks. Config dir target/agent/appdata-s2hp4s already holds settings.json (Remote named falador) and a workspace.json with one empty Project; reuse it. Launch with APPDATA pointed there and the environment stripped the way scripts/run-dev.ps1 does; drive it through ITS pipe (foreman-ctl-<pid>-*, listed from PowerShell with Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\), FOREMAN_PIPE set, FOREMAN_PROJECT_ID / FOREMAN_TERMINAL_ID unset, the exe you built as the CLI. Each attempt uses a NEW never-trusted directory under /tmp on the Remote. Never kill a process on the Remote you did not start. At the end: close your Sessions, stop YOUR instances by PID, remove your /tmp directories and their Claude transcripts, and remove only your own trust entries from the Remote's ~/.claude.json (verify the file round-trips before writing; otherwise list them).
Recording. Write a run log as you go (scratch file, not the repo): one line per run with wall-clock time, what you launched, what you did, and the observed outcome (snapshot text, status --json, room history, the agent's transcript on the Remote where that is the only proof a paste arrived). Summarise it as BEFORE and AFTER tables (runs, failures) in the commit body and in a new Results entry in the spec. Never print a token in the repo.
Hard rules: nothing may assume foreman, its skills or hook files exist on the Remote; a Remote agent may post chat, read history, read status and report hook events and nothing else; requests without any new field stay byte-identical on the wire, with a compat test; nothing under cfg(test) spawns a process or opens a socket outside the remote_probe network guard; do not detect agent state from screen text (see foreman-agent-state-campaign); do not launch Codex with its hook-trust bypass flag; do not mark anything on Grok or a Windows Remote as tested.

Blocked by: Stop losing held chat on a Remote Claude and make reconnect drivable
THIS CARD: Claude launches with no hold, and a hold nobody can see or open.
Defect 1. A Remote Claude that got no foreman hooks has no hold: `claude --settings <x> "<brief>"` (prompt_index refuses the shape, so the typed note goes out at Ready) types the note and its Enter into the folder-trust dialog, which answers "No, exit". The same holds for Grok and any Windows Remote, which cannot be tested here.
Defect 2. While chat is held nothing shows it (Session::chat_held is read only by tests) and the human cannot open it. The hold stays shut forever if curl is missing on the Remote, hooks are disabled there, the Claude is too old for SessionStart, or the hook lane drops the event (tunnel dispatch uses try_send on a bounded channel).
Step 1, reproduce BEFORE any fix, driving the real application:
 P1 `claude --settings '{}' "<multi-word brief>"` in a never-trusted directory, 5 runs: does Claude quit at the dialog?
 P2 a hold that never opens: launch a bare claude with the hook's curl unable to reach the Tunnel (for example a Remote PATH for that launch in which curl is absent, or another honest way you can show; do not uninstall anything on the Remote), answer the dialog, post to it, wait 60 s: is the post never delivered and is there any sign of it in the app? Record `status --json` for the Session.
Step 2, fix. Design decisions already made by the orchestrator on the human's behalf:
 a. Find out on the Remote whether Claude merges a second --settings (or another documented way to add hooks beside the user's own settings). If it does, a Claude launched with its own --settings gets foreman's hooks too and therefore the normal hold. If it does not, treat it as hookless (b).
 b. A hookless agent on a Remote (Claude without hooks, Grok, anything on a Windows Remote) gets NO typed note at launch: the note rides with its first chat delivery, the existing non-launch path of ReplyNote. Its chat delivery stays gated as today (Ready), because holding it with no signal would silently break unattended dispatch into trusted directories; say so plainly in docs/remote-sessions.md as a known limit. Do not add a hold that only a human can open for these.
 c. A human keystroke must NOT open a hold: the first keys a human presses are the ones that answer the trust dialog, and releasing then would type into it.
 d. A held Session shows it and offers an explicit release. `status --json` gains a field for it only when held (omitted otherwise, so today's output is byte-identical; compat test). In the GUI, show a quiet one-line cue on the held pane saying chat is held until the agent has started, with one action that delivers the held chat now. Follow foreman's existing conventions rather than inventing a component: read how the Remote Session disconnect bar is drawn and worded (commit 6b4926d and its follow-ups) and docs/settings-menu.md row grammar; proportional UI text, no sel_bg container, no new colour. Also expose the release as a local CLI verb or flag so it can be driven and tested (same wire rules; the Tunnel must not reach it). The cue must disappear the frame the hold opens.
 e. A dropped hook event must not strand a hold when a later event for the same connection arrives: any hook event that proves the agent is past its dialog opens an UntilStart hold; check what opens UntilPrompt and keep it safe.
Step 3, verify AFTER by driving the real application: P1 5 runs (Claude stays at the dialog, nothing typed, alive at 30 s; after answering, it can post back); P2 (the Session reports held in status --json; the CLI release delivers the held post in order exactly once; Claude replies). The GUI cue cannot be judged from the terminal: do not claim it looks right; state that it needs the human's eyes, and describe exactly what should be seen and where.
Notes from the card that just landed (commit afc3660; read its body first):
- The lost-input cause was found: after the trust dialog the Remote tty is in cooked mode until the REPL mounts, and Linux drops a line over 4095 bytes there. An UntilStart hold now opens remote::START_SETTLE (2 s) after SessionStart; any other hook event opens either hold at once. remote::hooked_claude is the one predicate for hooks and hold. Build on these; do not re-derive them.
- `foreman reconnect tN` now exists (local-only). Use it wherever a reconnect helps your verification.
- UntilPrompt has no fallback: a first argument that looks like a brief but never fires UserPromptSubmit (for example a subcommand such as claude mcp, or a slash command like /cost) holds chat until a reconnect. Your visible held state and explicit release (item d) are the answer to this; add it to P2's procedure: reproduce one such stuck hold BEFORE, and show AFTER that status --json reports it held and the release delivers.
- A slash brief containing whitespace still gets the reply note appended inside the slash command (remote::note_route; predates afc3660). Fix it here: a brief that starts with / (after leading whitespace) never carries the note in the prompt and takes the typed route under its hold. Table test, and one real run.
- The previous worker's run log format worked well (one line per run, then BEFORE/AFTER tables). Keep to it. When counting whether a post reached Claude from its transcript, count both typed prompts and queued_command attachments (a post that arrives while Claude is busy is queued, not lost).
Done when:
- BEFORE and AFTER records for P1 and P2 are in the commit body and the spec's Results
- no Remote launch of any agent types a note into the pane before a proven signal, except the documented hookless chat-delivery limit; pure-function table test for the per-agent choice
- held state is visible in status --json only when held (compat test), the release works from the CLI and the cue, order kept, nothing duplicated (unit tests)
- docs and both providers' dispatch skill copies say what is true; cite-guard clean; full suite passes
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
